problem_statement: Despite RAG’s success in reducing hallucinations and enabling up-to-date knowledge integration, emerging risks—including robustness failures, privacy leakage, adversarial attacks, and accountability gaps—threaten its real-world trustworthiness, and no unified framework exists to systematically address them.
core_contributions: Proposes a unified six-dimensional framework (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability) for analyzing trustworthiness in RAG systems
Provides structured taxonomies and evaluation protocols for each trustworthiness dimension, synthesizing over 200 works
Identifies cross-cutting research gaps and future directions, including synergies across dimensions and domain-specific deployment challenges
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on conceptual organization and literature synthesis; does not propose or evaluate novel algorithms or datasets.

evidence_spans.claim_value: six-dimensional framework (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability)
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We place our discussion around five key perspectives: reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, and accountability.

evidence_spans.claim_value: structured taxonomies and evaluation protocols for each trustworthiness dimension
evidence_spans.evidence_text: For each perspective, we present a general framework and taxonomy, offering a structured approach to understanding the current challenges, evaluating existing solutions, and identifying promising future research directions.

evidence_spans.claim_value: identifies cross-cutting research gaps and future directions
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Finally, we provide an in-depth discussion of future research directions for each aspect of trustworthiness, including promising directions within individual aspects and potential synergies across multiple areas.

problem_statement: Conventional RAG struggles with multi-source knowledge integration; GraphRAG is limited by noisy and incomplete graph structures.
core_contributions: Introduces GFM-RAG, the first graph foundation model (GFM) tailored for retrieval-augmented generation
Proposes a novel graph neural network architecture that reasons over graph structure to capture query-knowledge relationships
Demonstrates zero-shot generalization to unseen datasets without fine-tuning, enabled by two-stage training on large-scale knowledge graphs and documents
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on graph-structured knowledge integration in RAG; does not address unstructured or multimodal retrieval settings.

evidence_spans.claim_value: GFM-RAG is the first graph foundation model applicable to unseen datasets for retrieval without any fine-tuning required
evidence_spans.evidence_text: making it the first graph foundation model applicable to unseen datasets for retrieval without any fine-tuning required

evidence_spans.claim_value: GFM-RAG is powered by an innovative graph neural network that reasons over graph structure
evidence_spans.evidence_text: GFM-RAG is powered by an innovative graph neural network that reasons over graph structure to capture complex query-knowledge relationships

evidence_spans.claim_value: Trained on 60 knowledge graphs with over 14M triples and 700k documents
evidence_spans.evidence_text: The GFM with 8M parameters undergoes a two-stage training process on large-scale datasets, comprising 60 knowledge graphs with over 14M triples and 700k documents

problem_statement: Semantic-only RAG retrieves isolated, redundant chunks lacking intrinsic relationships, limiting LLM reasoning and response coherence.
core_contributions: Introduces KG2RAG: a novel RAG framework that leverages knowledge graphs to model fact-level relationships among retrieved text chunks.
Proposes KG-guided chunk expansion to diversify and enrich retrieval results beyond semantic similarity.
Designs KG-based context organization to structure retrieved chunks into coherent, paragraph-level inputs for LLMs.
limitations_or_scope: Evaluation limited to HotpotQA variants; KG construction relies on manual prompting of Llama-3; long-tail distribution of KG triplets per chunk may affect coverage.

evidence_spans.claim_value: KG2RAG uses knowledge graphs to provide fact-level relationships between chunks
evidence_spans.evidence_text: utilizes knowledge graphs (KGs) to provide fact-level relationships between chunks

evidence_spans.claim_value: KG-guided chunk expansion improves diversity and coherence of retrieved results
evidence_spans.evidence_text: KG2RAG employs a KG-guided chunk expansion process and a KG-based chunk organization process to deliver relevant and important knowledge in well-organized paragraphs
We conduct experiments on the benchmark dataset HotpotQA Yang et al. (2018)... In the distractor setting... In the fullwiki setting...

problem_statement: LLMs struggle with robust multi-hop reasoning over very long contexts when key facts are scattered—even with large context windows—due to lack of explicit retrieval and integration mechanisms.
model_tags: LLMs with long context support (e.g., >100k tokens)
core_contributions: Proposes a single-pass prompt engineering method that emulates RAG by combining relevance tagging and chain-of-thought reasoning within one LLM call.
Demonstrates improved accuracy on multi-fact QA tasks (e.g., object tracking, counting, indefinite knowledge) in long-context settings using BABILong.
Identifies critical prompt structure effects—especially instruction/question/context ordering—on long-context comprehension performance.
limitations_or_scope: Focused on synthetic long-context QA (BABILong); does not address real-world retrieval or domain-specific corpora; assumes model supports very long context windows.

evidence_spans.claim_value: emulates RAG via prompt engineering and chain-of-thought reasoning
evidence_spans.evidence_text: This paper addresses the challenge of comprehending very long contexts in Large Language Models (LLMs) by proposing a method that emulates Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) through specialized prompt engineering and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning.

evidence_spans.claim_value: evaluated on BABILong with distractor text and up to 64k tokens
evidence_spans.evidence_text: We evaluate on BABILong (Kuratov et al., 2024), a long-context QA benchmark derived from the classic bAbI tasks. The dataset interleaves large amounts of distractor text (PG19) with relevant question-answer pairs, creating contexts of up to tens of thousands of tokens.
These findings underscore that optimized prompt engineering, combined with guided reasoning, can enhance LLMs’ long-context comprehension...

problem_statement: Fragmented, non-unified tooling for retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG hinders reproducible comparison, fine-grained experimentation, and consistent benchmarking.
core_contributions: Introduces Rankify, a unified, modular, open-source Python toolkit for retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG
Provides prebuilt retrieval corpora, indexes, and benchmark datasets (e.g., Hugging Face reranking-datasets-light)
Supports diverse retrievers (sparse/dense/hybrid), state-of-the-art re-rankers, and end-to-end RAG pipelines with standardized evaluation
limitations_or_scope: Focuses on unifying existing methods rather than proposing novel retrieval/re-ranking algorithms; evaluation currently emphasizes Top-k accuracy and EM/recall/precision/containment, with MAP/NDCG planned for future versions.

evidence_spans.claim_value: Rankify is a unified, modular, open-source Python toolkit
evidence_spans.evidence_text: we introduce Rankify, a powerful and modular open-source toolkit designed to unify retrieval, re-ranking, and RAG within a cohesive framework

evidence_spans.claim_value: Provides prebuilt retrieval corpora, indexes, and benchmark datasets
evidence_spans.evidence_text: Rankify includes a collection of pre-retrieved datasets to facilitate benchmarking, available at Huggingface
Rankify supports a wide range of retrieval techniques, including dense and sparse retrievers, while incorporating state-of-the-art re-ranking models
